search_row.title: Haplodiploidy hypothesis for eusociality
search_row.statement: Because full sisters in haplodiploid species share three quarters of their genes, more than a mother shares with her offspring, haplodiploid insects are predisposed to evolve sterile worker castes.
search_row.math: with a singly mated queen, r_{sister,sister} = 3/4 > r_{mother,daughter} = 1/2, but r_{sister,brother} = 1/4

fields.dct:source: W. D. Hamilton (1964) The genetical evolution of social behaviour. II
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Use phylogenetic comparative analysis to test whether eusociality arises more often in haplodiploid than in diploid lineages after controlling for ancestral mating system.
fields.delphi:context: Formal status: the relatedness coefficients are proved. The explanatory claim is largely abandoned: the low sister-brother relatedness offsets the gain unless the sex ratio is biased, diploid termites are eusocial, and comparative work points to ancestral monogamy instead (Hughes et al. 2008).
